# Supplemental transition accounting for #603

The existing exact-final-HEAD cohort remains unchanged. Its scope omits merge-triggered runs on another SHA and earlier draft revisions. The new first-attempt overlap analyzer supplements, rather than replaces, that scope. It counts completed job intervals, their intersection while another run executed, and peak observed concurrency. It refuses foreign/duplicate job identities, incomplete reported rosters and multi-attempt input (use the existing attempt-lineage accounting instead). Active or growing inventories are lower bounds; no active job duration is guessed. Overlap is not a measured queue delay, a capacity claim, proof of causation or billed cost.

Reproduce after checking out this branch: `python .github/scripts/ci_transition_overlap.py .github/metrics/ci-transition-run-45421145394-20261124.json .github/metrics/ci-transition-run-45437716141-20261124.json`.
Local fixture suite: `python -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p test_ci_transition_overlap.py -v` (5 methods passed, including 9 negative controls). The stored report was calculated independently from the provider intervals in the connector, using the same sweep-line definition; the Python CLI has been tested on fixtures, not these exact remote JSON bytes. The source and tests match the locally tested Git blob IDs. Once both runs terminate, capture new immutable snapshots and run the CLI against them; do not overwrite this observation. Record workflow queue and scheduling data separately. No production workflow changes or new CI runs.
